System Permission Guide

1. Microphone

Purpose: capture voice when you speak in voice chat. Requested when you actively turn on your microphone. If denied or disabled, you cannot send voice but can continue listening and using features that do not need sound capture. Minimizing a room may keep an active audio session running. Turn off the microphone or leave the room to stop it.

2. Camera

Video broadcasting is hidden in the current version and camera permission is not actively requested. If video features are introduced, this explanation will be updated first and system permission requested when you actively use them.

3. Photo selection

Purpose: use the system photo picker to choose a photo for your avatar. The app does not scan the entire photo library; choosing a photo does not authorize access to other library content.

Only an avatar you confirm saving is uploaded. It is converted to static JPEG, resized and stripped of metadata. You can choose a preset avatar or cancel photo selection. These choices do not affect voice chat or private messaging features that do not require photos.

4. Notifications

Purpose: show private-message, follow, voice-room start and safety alerts on signed-in devices and update necessary badges. Alerts may by default show the sender’s nickname, private message text or an interaction summary, without photos or image content. Enable “Hide Message Content” under Settings → Notifications in the app to use generic wording for later alerts. iOS notification settings control lock-screen and banner previews. Requested on first use after you agree to the current documents and complete a lightweight connectivity check, before Apple sign-in. The request is not repeated after a system decision exists. Denial or authorization failure does not prevent sign-in; you can request permission later from the enable option in message or notification settings. Before sign-in, the app only asks for system authorization; it does not register with APNs, upload device tokens or create account bindings. When the system framework returns a device push token, it is associated only with the current valid account session that has agreed to the documents.

You may deny notifications or change allowed notifications, sounds, banners and badges in iOS Settings → Notifications → kikitalk. You can also turn off alerts for the current account in the app. Denial does not affect in-app messages or voice chat; turning off alerts does not delete in-app messages. The system or network may delay or fail to deliver alerts.

5. Managing permissions and other information

Find kikitalk in iOS Settings to manage granted permissions such as the microphone, or use the corresponding Privacy & Security category. Revoking a system permission does not affect prior lawful processing. Use the app’s relevant setting to withdraw service privacy consent.

The app does not currently request contacts, location or advertising tracking permissions, or local network permission for ordinary public internet connections. Before consent, it obtains and verifies the latest complete text only through the public legal-document interface of our account service, without account credentials, cookies, device identifiers or push tokens. It creates no account and starts no audio/video or notification service. Only after first agreeing does it access the account service health check to test connectivity, also without account credentials, cookies or push tokens. The system may ask you to choose wireless data access; whether a prompt appears is controlled by the device. System push is used only when you allow notifications and enable the relevant alerts. Local image caches and Keychain credential storage are not granted through these sensitive-permission prompts. See the Privacy Policy at https://kiki.group/privacy/ for information handling, deletion and feedback. Operator: Li Hao (李浩). Contact: 2114581274@qq.com.
